sources.name: ArchDaily
sources.summary: In many Asian cities, the summer climate can increasingly be experienced from a distance. In Hong Kong , it is possible to move from an apartment tower through a podium mall , enter the Mass-Transit-Railway system (MTR), arrive beneath another commercial complex, and continue through enclosed footbridges or underground passages while encountering remarkably little of the atmosphere outside. Heat, humidity, rain, and seasonal variation remain present, but they can be largely bypassed through a continuous network of conditioned interiors.
